These have been floating around recently so I thought I'd put them in one spot in the hopes they get some more visibility. Individually they're pretty situational but combined they show up all the time, so it's good to have them under your belt. These all assume that the first spider is "dealt with", meaning it's behind you and is either running away from you or is far enough away that it won't hit you when you cdash. I gave 'em lil names just to distinguish.

- **Calli Slash**: if the spider is running away from you and you're to the left of it, forward slash and instantly cdash. The combined damage of the nail hit and the cdash will kill the spider. Found by calligraphiti 
- **GOAT Slash**: if the spider is running toward you and you're to the left of it, up slash and instantly cdash. Same idea as Calli Slash with the bonus of the up slash turning the spider around. I'm not a 1432+ runner but I've been told this is worth with those spider patterns. Found by JaGOAT
- **Reverse GOAT Slash**: if the spider is running toward you and you're to the right of it, up slash and instantly cdash (helps to go neutral just before the up slash to line it up). Uses the same turnaround tech as GOAT Slash but from the other side, so you don't go through the spider. Found by me :3

Keep in mind that if the spider is far enough right to turn around on its own these are generally not advised.

PSA about geo routing (particularly negotiating Spire geo, Lever geo, and Herrah Rock geo):

The colors on the last table represent the "tiers" of money, where green is fastest but gets you the least, yellow is average on both, and red is slowest but gives the most. They're ordered in this way because Herrah Rock + Lever is roughly equivalent to Spire (~30-35 geo).

So, from this the strats are:
1) **If you're filthy rich (531 is the minimum assuming you pick up all the geo that drops) coming out of GHusk, Lever geo in Chandelier and in Lantern is the fastest.**
2) **For all other cases, start with Spire geo in Chandelier and get Lever geo in Lantern. If you have an extra cast after Spire Geo then also collect Lever geo in Chandelier. If you still don't have enough, get Herrah Rock geo after.** Lever in Chandelier isn't worth if you're gonna get Herrah Rock after since it's faster to just get Spire in Chandelier and skip Herrah Rock, but the opposite is true for Lantern.

So this is a set up for the low% stallball that has been used for a while, but I dont think anyone has published it yet on strats.
With this set up you have 2 frames to shoot the fb at the end instead of just 1, which helps a lot. 

In terms of the set up itself, you have to stand (dont hold any directions) against the wall, hold left and jump once you reach the highlighted part of the grass (see image), if you hear some kind of landing sound, continue with the trick and fb around there (see image), if you dont hear anything strange, turn right, stand still against the wall and repeat the set up. 
This works on both 1.5 and 1.4, the window when you can jump is pretty tight (1 frame), but it makes the trick easier overall.

An update to this post.
It turns out that you can make the set up easier if you stand still against the wall, nail slash twice without holding any direction, press and hold left and, one frame after the left input, press and hold jump. The rest is the same as before.
To do this consistantly you just have to press the left key and the jump key one after the other as fast as possible (if you go for this keep in mind that this feels almost the same as pressing them at the same time, but if both inputs are on the same frame, the trick wont work) and check for the weird landing sound before commiting to the fb. Here is an example of a successful and a non successful attempt, the trick with hitboxes for better understanding of it and a slow motion segment of the set up change.

soul collection for isma entrance skip
Your goal here is to fill up your soul meter and clear out everything below the red line (including inflated hwurmps that might enter and get hit by your fireball). If you kill enemies while executing the skip you get freeze frames and will always fail. (img 1) Ideally you want to enter with 3 soul, but it's possible to enter with no soul (if you failed a spike tunnel skip).

 (img 2) is your ideal case scenario. Execution shown here https://youtu.be/bAro622-PE0?t=69. Numbers denote the order in which you kill the hwumrps. You need 6 soul so pogo (1) and slash (2) 5 times. If you need more than 6 soul keep going according to numbers. you don't need to kill (3) since it is high enough to not interfere with your skip execution, so just hit it however many times you need. Number 4 is always killed last because you need to kill him if inflated because you cannot take chances with letting him bounce because he will get hit by your fireball.

(img 3) or its variations is the most common encounter I think, you need to clear out (1) and (2) and sometimes (4) if it hangs low enough. Start by nailing (1) or (2) - they will almost always both inflate, just keep nailing until they're both dead. If they don't both inflate, kill the one closer to you and then the other. With any luck it might drift close to the acid so it can be one-shot.

If while entering you get the opportunity to pogo (4) into the acid, do so immediately, this is always beneficial. 

Sometimes while dealing with (1) and (2), (3) or (4) might start drifting towards you and you need to react to avoid taking damage. In that case almost always the best solution is to fireball the inflated hwurmps because taking damage often means you dunk too and lose time. So whenever you see you're about to take damage use your fireballs.

For any other variations use your best judgment. Your soul backup is top left, dreamnail the rotten egg thing.

You can also try to slash earlier after the 2 jumps if you are having trouble hiting the one on top right away or with gruzzers on the ceiling having 8 health or to slash a bit later to try to hit 5th and 6th gruzzers more often, again, your preference.

Backup wallcling storage setup for blue lake. Can potentially be faster than 1 slash by as much as .4 if you minihop instead of fulljumping, but it's pretty inconsistent then.

**LK Dash Attack Storage**
If you stagger Lost Kin during its aerial dash attack animation, it skips the landing phase and still thinks it's supposed to dash. Even if it pulls an empty hop or down stab, air dash always overrides them. You can manipulate this to chain air dash triples multiple times with the right timing. (s/o to Magnetic Pizza for helping me figure this out lol)

In order for the dash attack to be stored, Lost Kin needs to be staggered during the "Dash Attack" animation (green circle). If it enters the "In Air" animation (red circle), it loses the storage. Getting the third fireball tick to hit lost kin before the animation ends is a bit tricky, so watch the video on the left and practice the timing. You want to shoot the fireball at about the same time as LK starts the dash - just be careful because if you shoot too early you'll single hit. Even when you're not in the stagger lock, be on the lookout for the air dash attack and see if you can stagger during the dash animation - the dash anticipate animation lasts a long time so make sure it's not staggered until the dash starts to get the storage.

The video on the right shows an alternate stagger rotation that could be viable for LP. The extra nail hit will get the stagger count up to 7 after the triple, and on 1.2.2.1 it will still get tripled fairly consistently. However, it can be awkward/rng to triple the air dash with the extra stagger hit, so I would recommend only trying that on later patches. 

When the dash attack is stored, Lost Kin can do a grounded dash 28% of the time which is worse than an aerial dash because you can't keep the storage (at least not consistently) but you can still triple it if you fireball early enough.

After breaking the wall by archives, cdashing into the upper fog canyon room instead of dashing through is ~1.5 seconds faster for True Ending and ~0.9 faster for All Skills [1]. The cdash will work in the following situations:
- If the ooma is high enough, the cdash will kill it and knock the core towards the transition and doesn't hit you (this is the most common)
- The ooma is very low and you can cdash right above it 

If the ooma is high enough that your cdash will hit it but low enough that it'll get knocked into the wall, attempting to cdash through the room will result in a hefty damage tank which loses 0.1 to cdashless [2]. This is especially punishing in TE where being 3 HP for No Eyes up to the toll bench sucks, but you can react to the ooma position and cancel the cdash to avoid the damage tank (also applicable to AS and 106%):
- The most safe option is to cancel the cdash early, then shade dash through it and do a minimum height wings [3]. This loses 0.05 to cdashless but saves 0.05 to damage tanking. To avoid floaty wings from the dream gate, do a jump wings during dash cooldown in the previous room which loses nothing if done correctly.
- Alternatively, you can wait until your cdash hits the ooma and cancel cdash on reaction, then quickly wings and shade dash through the explosion [4]. This saves 0.05 to cdashless and 0.15 to damage tanking, but is considerably harder and riskier so I wouldn't default to this especially in TE. However, this can be used as a backup if you try to cdash above it but misjudge its position and get hit, so you can afford to be less cautious about going through with the cdash. (Do note that you have to react to hitting the ooma, NOT the ooma core hitting the wall. If you wait that long it'll be too late to cancel the cdash, so there is still a level of proactivity required for this strat, you just have more time to make the decision.)

After the discussion that prompted the split of the Any% NMG ComSoB sheet, I started talking to CC about the last devout's FSM and theoretically optimal variations of the quick kill. In CC's words, the FSM briefly is:
> 1) Devout wakes up
> 2) Devout waits for up to 1s randomly for the knight to enter melee range before deciding to go forward; otherwise it'll start walking forward until it reaches melee range
> 3) If it walked forward it'll wait up to 0.5s to attack or walk backwards; if it didn't its up to 1.5s (attack/walk backwards is 50/50)
> So a VERY important thing is that you NEVER cross the melee part of the devout on your own, ALWAYS wait for it to walk forward

So from this we want a setup that:
1) Wakes the devout up as soon as possible
2) Encourages the devout to walk into you as soon as possible
3) Keeps you actionable when the devout does walk into you so you can chase it if needed to stay in its melee range and prevent a reroll

CC's suggestion is `Fireball -> Dash -> Fireball -> Dash -> Fireball`, with a bit of walking forward before the last fireball to get a bit closer to the devout's melee range (first clip). You'll then want to walk toward the devout if its either currently moving at you or has moved far enough to get you in its melee range, indicated by it stopping in front of you after walking at you (second clip). If it walks up to you then backs up, as mentioned above, do NOT walk toward it until it starts moving toward you again.

The last thing is that the devout can attack too early for you to fit four nail slashes while it's open. If this does happen, you'll wanna do a slight variation that saves the last slash for a second open, which you can force with a slash (third clip). Conveniently the extra damage from this cancels the freeze frames, making the strat lose about 0.6s-0.7s to an optimal quick kill. If you're low though you can just back up before slashing.

Just an update post for the wcs in Ancestral Mound with a good visual cue.  The easiest way to set it up is with the nail knockback inventory cancel.  If the Knight's eye is mostly visible aside from the bottom right, then you are at the correct distance.  Ideally the Baldur lands on the platform so you can pogo it.  If he doesn't, then, with some practice, you should hopefully be able to get it within a couple tries.

## -------- Phases ------
THK has 1000 HP, or 1250 HP (he heals TO, not adding 250 after entering phase 4 (last))

phase 1: 1000-751 HP
phase 2 (when he is able to do the first scream): 750-401 HP
phase 3 (where he is able to do 2nd scream/self stab): 400 until death HP (doesn't end until you hit him AFTER he has reached 0 or less HP, the hit that ends this phase does damage to the phase 4 health pool (ex. if you end phase with a nail slash he will be at 245hp in phase 4))
phase 4: 250-0
## ------- Evade Antic --------- (backdash/parry)
before THK's idle animation (explained below), THK will roll an RNG check depending on the phase he is in
**(phase 1: 0%, 2: 60%, 3: 15%, 4: 0%)**
if this check succeeds, he will either parry or backdash (50/50) after checking whether or not to turn around ( the only thing that can delay the parry/backdash is if he is turning around. )
the evade rng check is also retriggered by the end of a parry, as that goes to the idle, (this could be the cause of parrys chaining into themselves). this isnt the only way for thk to parry, or backdash
## **------- THK idle animation -------**
### This is the animation/state after he wakes up from a stagger, after he finishes a move, etc.

**exception 1:** the end of a backdash does not enter the idle animation, it just immediately goes to another attack (after this attack ends it will go to idle.) .
**exception 2:** an attack immediately after a teleport also does not usually enter the idle animation, it just immediately goes to another attack (after this attack ends it will go to idle.) not entirely sure about this one
### The amount of time he spends in the idle state is rng and phase dependent:
Phase 1: .75s to 1s
Phase 2: .25s to .5s
Phase 3: 0s to .25s
Phase 4: 1 second

Hornet staggers on 1.5 will consistently break on high fps. This is because the code to check for ground collisions starts too soon, since the state advances on next graphics not physics frame.

There is definitely some t-ft work at play here (this is literally the measurement of time between graphics and physics frames here) and 1.5 for whatever reason is unique in that at 50 fps hornet virtually never breaks, since capping in a half hour of testing i've had 0 breaks compared to infinite at 165. However testing on 1.2.2.1 indicates hornet still breaks at 50 fps, and it would be much more inconvenient anyway to lower fps.

The end conclusion being that dropping ur fps for hornet while not necessarily optimal yields some interesting results. The main drawback is that menuing loses about 0.2-0.3 if optimized and you'd need to do it twice, however for slopeball categories where you might be incentivized to run 50 fps anyway it could be interesting, as well as vsync categories like 112 where you would be able to be uncapped for KP and thus only lose time for one of the menus, or you could just do left side and only have one menu.

Each double can either save 0.2s or 1.2s, theres some math behind doubles here but essentially the average timesave per double is 0.7s, however it lets you stunlock hornet way more consistently. If you get even one more double the menuing is worth it.

The video shows hornet breaking when in frame by frame, which is very consistent, and then unbreaking at full speed

TLDR: at a top level turning on in game cap on patch 1.5 for hornet prevents her from breaking, probably saves time on average even if its inconvenient

Broken Vessel has 525hp; stagger values are 9 hits for combo (<1s/hit) and 13 otherwise; headbanging phase starts for the first time once you deal 155 damage, so 4 shade soul hits is always enough to trigger it.

You want to always start the fight by firing 2 shade souls (where you do a small jump between the first fb and the second one), which has a few different outcomes:
-both shade souls double or one triples and the other singles (e.g. whilst bv is on the ground or dashing towards you):
For this case get 4 nail hits before the headbanging phase starts*, and then you want to get 1 nail, 1 pogo and a ddark, followed by 1 upslash, one pogo and another ddark, followed by a pogo and a ddark, finally ending with a ddark. 

-only one shade soul doubles and two single hit:
For this case there's pretty much no risk of staggering before the headbanging phase starts, so try to get 7/8 nail hits in and then do your first ddark. After that you want to do a sequence of 1 upslash, 1 pogo and a ddark (all) twice, which will send the boss into a staggered state. Depending on wether you got 7 or 8 nail hits at the beginning you can either directly ddark the boss (or shade soul double if you're feeling spicy) or you'll have to do a pogo into the ddark.

The two most common cases are the ones described above, but there are some other misc starts to the fight, for example, where you get "bad rng" but the 3rd shade soul doubles (or even triples in some cases) or you try to go for three doubles. Essentially, if you get 5 shade soul hits at the start of the fight you want to follow the 1double2singles case (soul gathering a little less strict), but instead of finishing with a ddark you can get enough soul for a last shade soul.
*try not going for more than 4 because stagger is at 9 combo hits (or 3 hits if you start with 5 shade soul hits)

I really didnt find the existing set up for the slopeball easy at all, and from my understanding, neither do many ppl, esp for shamans. Thats the reason why i've been looking for a more consistent (and hopefully faster) way of setting it up.

To begin with, you are going to line yourself up with the edge of the platform (or run up to it), then you are going to dash making sure you still have your aerial dash, then you dash again once you reach that line (1st image). Afterwards, you need to pogo as high as possible (you can use the horizontal line (2nd picture) as a reference, but you have 4f to pogo). To finish it up, you need to dash as high as you can (this roughly lines up with the beginning of the root, but i found it more comfortable to just dash at the peak of the pogo) and then shortly after the dash ends you need to fb.

The most common mistakes i've found are not dashing close enough to the edge of the platform, pogoing too late / too early, delaying too much the dash (its not super precise, but it can happen), fbing too late (this also isnt too precise) and doing the final dash up to the platform too low (the wiggle room for this will obs depend on how well you did the rest). Most of this will either cause you to not reach the platform or to simply not get the slopeball, depending on how well you perform the rest.

Its also worth mentioning that you can try to back it up by replicating the skip starting from the pogo.

A set of strats to make the big darkroom in deepnest consistent and fast for 1221 low%.

All the walking spiders spawn in the same spot facing left or right, and activate when you enter a certain radius (The first 2 activate upon room entry). This means that consistent movement between activation and encountering a spider leaves you with 2 possible positions for each.

You want to make sure you walljump twice on the right side in the beginning, to activate the 3rd spider as late as possible. Walljumping off of the left wall activates it early and gives worse positions, if you jump too high even one jump on the left can activate it.

The first set of 2 spiders has two easy ways to deal with them, shown in video 2 and 3. The way to tell which to do is whether you see a spider as you do your 2nd walljump or not. After them I upslash in case the weaverling spawned quickly.

Spider 3 can be dealt with as shown in video 2 and 3. It's possible to not get hit by the rng in video 3, but it's precise and hard to do in the dark.

Spider 4 is fireballed for 15 geo, as long as you aren't too slow from the activation range you shouldn't miss any.

Spider 5 can be dealt with easily by doing two full jumps from the darkest pole in the background.

Spider 6 will be in the corner where you wanna go up half the time, so walking off and pogoing twice gets you up to the wall without having to worry if it's there (the 2nd pogo is hitting the spikes under the breakable floor). This is the only strat that can be a little bit sketchy, since you only have a few frames to pogo before you fall into the spikes and get reset to the start of the room.

The movement shown in the first video showcases all of put together.
The image shows which spider I'm referring to with each number, and the line of the same color is their approximate activation range.

**New Optimal False Knight Strats for LP**

On LP, False Knight will do a rollback after being staggered, unless they both get staggered to the left and are on or close to the ground. This rollback loses 0.5s. A damage tank loses 0.3 in freeze frames. This means the following for cats where you full kill FK (if you do not full kill FK, the only change is that you do the damage tank and left stagger Phase 1 on small jump back):

On the pattern where FK jumps up at the start, you do phase 1 as normal. You can then stagger them to the left in phase 2 by walking through them, as shown in the video. **You must delay the last nail here until FK turns back around**, or else they will stagger with the head turned the wrong way, which is timeloss for next phase. Then you do the same thing in phase 3, except don't delay the last nail as for last phase it does not matter where the head is turned. **This saves about 0.1 to normal strats, AND is less punishing if you miss a nail in Phase 2 and 3 as you don't get hit a second time if you miss a nail**. 

When FK does a small jump back, you do the damage tank as in the video and walk through them. This cancels FKs jump, making this Phase 1 very easy and consistent. You then do Phase 2 and Phase 3 the same as on the first pattern I mentioned (so do the walk through thing). **This saves at least 0.3 to current strats, but realistically more than that as any frame FK jumps up on the second jump is lost twice, as they also have to come back down from it to start the head popout-animation**

For the big jump back, and then another jump back you do the fight as normal except Phase 3, where you do the walk through thing with no delay on last nail and **save 0.5**. This is also in one of the clips.

For big jump back and then a jump up, you stagger to the left in Phase 1, then do the same that the first two patterns I mentioned do, **saving 0.1**

There's been debate over whether using analog left or digital left is better for 1 slash, and there are cases for both. 

Using analog left increases your max fallspeed, meaning the window to clear the ledge is tighter, but if you do clip the ledge, since you'll continue walking right you can sometimes keep the WCS anyway. 

Using digital left increases this window, but I've also noticed it tends to turn you to the left when you enter the water if you continue holding it, which can also eat your jump for some reason, so you either have to eat this timeloss or stop holding the WCS before entering the water. 

Switching between digital and analog, as shown in the clip, should give you the best of both worlds. You get some reduced fallspeed on the first dash by holding digital left, then switch to analog in case you clip the ledge and so you don't turn when entering the water.

So i realized I was losing quite a bit of time to the pair of husks at the end of the last fb skip room and labbed the best way to deal with them. First, it's important to note that they have a fixed spawn position and they only pick a direction and start moving once you get close enough to them. The right one (Husk Bully) starts moving roughly while you are casting your 2nd fb, and the left one (Wandering Husk) once you're a bit past the fb skip (this efectively means that, if you miss the fb skip, only the Husk Bully will have started moving early).

The husks can also do random delays, so apart from the 4 main patterns (LL, LR, RL and RR) you'll still need to adapt a little bit to what they do. The clips show how to optimally respond to each pattern in that order, but here are some extra notes:
 - If the Wandering Husk goes left, its pretty important to recognize if you'll fit in between him and the lowest part of the ceiling (i also put an image of what hitboxes look like) by just pogoing over him. If you don't think thats the case, you'll need to do a left slash before the pogo (loses about 0.25)(1st clip), sometimes you can get unlucky enough to the point that you'll need to kill him or dmg tank to the left on the previous husk if you recognize it quickly enough.

- For the RL pattern (3rd clip) the idea with the movement is to barely squeeze past the lowest part of the arch and both husks. You can sometimes get a little stuck on the arch and that's still a lot better than dmg tanking.

Inconsistent but reactable setup to get WCS in the room before Xero when leaving RG. Could save up to 0.5 depending on chains. Loses 0-2 frames if failing the good way and ~0.18 worst case.

Enter the room and have the correct t-ft to get control on the earlier possible frame. Neutral dash, start holding left, and keep buffering dashes. Release left during the fourth dash. If you didn't have a dash delayed by a frame from t-ft, two more neutral dashes will put you in the right spot to have corner WCS.

You can determine if you got control on the correct frame only losing 1-2 frames. Enter neutral, try to dash, then immediately start holding left. If your dash works, you should be able to tell whether it was from the correct frame. If you didn't dash, you'll only lose however much time you were neutral for. If you're really a gamer and can consistently dash on exactly the right frame and then press left exactly the next frame, you can probably do this while losing 0 time.

If you did get the dash from the correct place, you'll need to check if you're still aligned at the end of the 4th dash, since you sometimes need to wait an extra frame before dashing due to fcr. If the knight is touching the foreground pole, you're in the wrong spot and should do the rest of the room normally. If the knight is not touching the pole, you will always have WCS after doing two neutral dashes and jumping. It works about 2/3 of the time for me, but it's been streaky so its hard to measure. If you're in the wrong spot, you will spend 0.3 neutral, but you get some of this time back at the end of the room since you can dash. It ends up losing around 0.18. If you can manage to notice if you lost a frame dashing, you could theoretically try this strat with no time loss if it fail.

I've seen many ppl struggle with this epogo, when in reality its very lenient and can become very consistent with some practice. In this post I'll be explaining what goes into making the skip works in the hopes that ppl can improve at it. First of all, [here's](https://youtu.be/iZk3jUqFHGA) a vid of me doing the skip many times in a row to show what kind of variance can be expected and still have the trick work.

In order to perform the skip you want to hardfall and do a full jump shortly after regaining control (this isn't super tight, so its best to not greed it too much, as you can't buffer the jump out of the hardfall). You want to stop holding left a fair bit before the left wall (to ensure you don't go on top of it) and then start holding left again once you are safely past the ledge. I find that slashing when i reach this mushroom in the foreground to start heading right setps up the spore pretty well (the spore bounces on the wall and then follows you left quite well past the wall, its very important that this is the case). You then want to pogo at mid height (too low or too high can make the trick a little more akward, but its not too tight) and start holding left inmediatly. After this point you want to focus on not bonking the ceiling after the pogo, so you want to use your fbs to gain as much distance as possible (also not very tight, but imagine it as some sort of fb skip). Once you are past the right wall (assuming you didn't bonk on the ceiling) you can start holding right for a bit to ensure you dmg tank. Nearly any dmg tank at this point will allow you to clear the gap (in the vid im at 300fps and i have no problem clearing the gap), so you really just want to make sure you don't dodge the explosion.

For folks that run without in-game music on, here are some setups for dashing through the gate as it opens. The first is for a kill with VS and the second is with a nail (since this will affect nail cooldown). This takes some practice to get used to the freezeframes; using the WK flipping back animation gave me a better feel for it. For the second setup, I wouldn't recommend buffering a jump out of the dash since it can come up just a little short if timed perfectly.

Timing from the kill rather than the death animation is necessary to be fully consistent since, like Gruzmother, WK count as dead as soon as you land the final hit (which is what the gate timing is based on), but their death animation depends on how exactly they're killed (e.g. having to fall if killed midair, or not doing the flip back if the last hit is a pogo).
